    Singular-pair orientation for BGRS Figure 16 #

    A singular length-two ray path has representatives with nonzero ordinary composite, but its special BGRS product is zero. The special relation therefore gives a nonzero middle-Jacobson sandwich. Transferring that sandwich to any zero representative pair shows that the ordinary left factor allows transit and the ordinary right factor allows cotransit.

    Because the ray quiver is reversed, this says that the packaged second arrow allows transit while the packaged first arrow does not. Consequently two singular pairs cannot share an arrow in opposite positions. Figure 16 only has to exclude sharing in the same position (up to duality, one case).

                The load-bearing Roiter step in BGRS 4.5. If a literal zero pair f * g = 0 retains the exceptional nonzero middle-radical sandwich, then inserting a radical parameter tau = pi(Y,Y) makes the composite nonzero.

                Indeed, if both the constant and linear tau sandwiches vanished, polynomial generation of End(Y) and Roiter's square alternative would kill every middle-endomorphism sandwich: degrees at least two lie in Jac(End Y)^2. This contradicts the retained nonzero radical sandwich.

                      Opposite-position sharing is impossible: the first arrow of a singular pair cannot be the second arrow of another singular pair.
